theme: Review Output Selection and Side-Effect Safety

shots.title: Require explicit retrospective scorecard selection (#583)
shots.notes: Review discovers canonical scorecards centrally, permits implicit selection only when exactly one exists, supports --sprint, and fails with a concrete recovery command when history is ambiguous.

shots.title: Scope review output and side effects to the selected sprint (#583)

hazards.description: Removing latest-card guessing also required updating the built-in workflow, completion guidance, and agent recommendations so mature repositories retained an executable command.

Independent architecture review found that the PostToolUse guard could reintroduce cross-sprint gate mutation and that three runtime guidance surfaces still emitted the obsolete bare command. Both findings were fixed and independently re-reviewed.

shots.notes: Default output is adjacent to the selected scorecard, status text is emitted on stderr, and historical review generation cannot complete a different active sprint's review gate.

conditions.description: The legacy implicit-latest behavior was embedded in both the command and its workflow consumers, so the contract change needed cross-surface validation.

training.description: A write-producing command must not infer its target from a directory containing durable history.
training.outcome: Ambiguous review selection now fails closed and offers explicit path and sprint selectors.

training.description: Artifact generation and lifecycle mutation are separate side effects with separate scope checks.
training.outcome: Historical review output stays historical and does not satisfy the current sprint's gate.

training.description: Machine-readable stdout must not be contaminated by operational status messages.
training.outcome: Review markdown remains on stdout while write confirmation goes to stderr.

training.description: A direct-command boundary fix is incomplete until hook-driven mutation paths and every generated invocation are reviewed independently.
training.outcome: The independent reviewer caught and verified repairs for the PostToolUse gate path and remaining runtime consumers.

nutrition.description: Focused review, workflow, agent, and completion suites passed: 138 tests across six files.
The complete Vitest suite passed after the focused contract tests.
Typecheck and build passed, including packages/pi-extension.
Roadmap validation passed and review requirements were persisted before closeout.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: A small CLI ambiguity exposed a broader rule: durable historical artifacts need explicit identity at every write boundary.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: When making selection stricter, search every generated command and workflow step that depended on the old default.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: The output-path bug and the gate-mutation bug shared the same missing selected-sprint identity.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: The roadmap focus API can apply the same explicit-identity rule to bounded planning context.

bunker_locations: Never select a write target by latest-file convention when more than one durable artifact exists.
Status messages for stdout-capable commands belong on stderr.
Historical artifact generation must not mutate the active sprint unless sprint identities match.
When tightening a CLI contract, update all workflow-generated invocations in the same sprint.
yardage_book_updates: src/cli/commands/review.ts centralizes scorecard discovery and explicit path/sprint selection.
Review output defaults beside the selected scorecard and only matching active sprint gates are updated.
Built-in workflow, agent guidance, and completion guidance pass --sprint explicitly.
course_management_notes: Focused and full validation passed; the branch is pushed but no merge is implied.
The recommended independent architecture review requested changes, verified the follow-up, and approved the end-to-end historical/current sprint boundary.
